The sentence is not an answer. He is the first person in four hundred miles to look at this line and he is not permitted to learn anything a rod would have told him and the chapter has to survive that.**
2. **The woman of about fifty at the shut gate may not be asked anything, by anybody, including the protagonist, and no chapter may send anybody to her for any reason.**

4. **The four days of notice is the instrument, and all five of this volume's notices are on a page, in Chapters 0326, 0327, 0328, 0329 and 0335, and every one of them is four days.** A notice on any other day is a three-day instrument and a three-day instrument does not fail, it arrives warm. **This batch writes no notice and may not be the one that reduces one.**
5. **A weekday is a figure and day 1 is a Tuesday and no chapter may take a weekday from a neighbouring chapter, from the table above, from a card, or from a state file — and no chapter may use an ordinal for a month.**
6. **An elapsed count is this chapter's own day number subtracted from the day the thing happened, and the day a thing happened has to be opened in a file and not remembered, and a derived value may not be attributed to a chapter or to a mouth.** **Batch 0004 found and repaired twenty such figures in ten chapters and the finding is published in its record §9; a fifth batch that finds none should suspect that it did not look.**
7. **The Crown's schedule is on a page in this volume and is standing and correct and is never opened, never filled in, never withdrawn, and never the subject of a chapter. The sheet the man of about forty-one in a very good coat will not turn over is not the schedule.**
8. **Nobody in this batch gets stronger. Adrian is Stage 2. He performs no working, no threshold is opened, the Narrow Mark is not opened a third time, the other world is not named once, nobody offers him a workway and he asks for none, and the words *passage* and *privilege* are at zero across the ten chapters and are not the words to reach for.**

## The ten days, and what each one has to carry

**These are the beats the volume outline put on the day map at §14.3 and they are constraints and not a plan for the prose. Chapter 0342 and Chapter 0346 are fixed to their days by `outline/volume-07.md` §10, §11 and §14.3 and by the four decisions of record, and a writer who cannot make a beat work in a room with a date on the door has a worse day than a writer who moves a beat, provided the day, the weekday, the month day, the word, the cloth and the prohibitions hold.**

1. **0341, day 341, a Saturday, the twenty-sixth. Character and relationship, and the volume's last run at a gate.** **The woman of about fifty at the shut gate and the man of about thirty-eight with the barrow are in this chapter and in Chapter 0347 and in no others.** **She gives no name and no name may be given her, and she may not be asked anything by anybody including the protagonist, and no chapter may send anybody to her for any reason.** Her second handle is a brass key on a tarred cord in the apron pocket, a bar of ash in two brackets, a wooden hook, a piece of chalk, and a date in chalk on the post every morning with nothing rubbed out. **The chapter's job is to show that she is not asked and that the not-asking has a cost and that the cost is not hers, and that the one thing only she and the man with the barrow know is not said in this chapter and is not said in any chapter of this volume.** **A man with a barrow is in the chapter and the reader knows he has something and the room does not, and the chapter does not explain it and does not hint at it in a way that explains it.**
2. **0342, day 342, a Sunday, the twenty-seventh. THE CLIMAX.** **The room over a market, in daylight, with a date in chalk on the door, and about nine people in it.** **The word the man of about thirty-four said in Chapter 0310 comes off the register-keeper's second slate, in chalk, with a cloth, by the man who said it, in front of the same about nine people, and after this the reader has been told what the line in the orchard is called and no page in the world can say so.** **He has no standing to take anything back: he is barred from every roster at his own request, and the instrument that removes a word from a page in this world is a room, in daylight, with a date on it, and a person, and it is not enough, and a person may not be removed by it at all.** **His reason is four sentences long and it is his and it may not be improved on: a name is only a place somebody can be taken to when somebody is going to go, and there is a man with a barrow in this city who is going to go, and he will not have a word on that slate for a thing a man is about to put a barrow against.** **The protagonist is in the room and is not asked one question about it. The register-keeper has the slate and Tamsin Quill is not in the room. Nobody asks the man of about twenty-five whether it will go, and his nine words are not said.** **What is not in the chapter and may not be put in it: no working, no threshold, no panel, no mark, no office, no title, no stage, no spent passage privilege, and no improvement on anything said on day 137, day 154, day 250, day 275, day 294, day 298 or day 300. The ninth line is not moved, dated, read aloud or resolved. The board is not written on. Nobody puts a boot on the nine feet and nobody opens the bag and nobody says what a wage in salt is worth and Break is not open. And the day-154 sentence is in no mouth in this chapter and is not paraphrased and is not improved on in any direction — what is in the chapter instead is a hand in a cloth and four sentences that are the man's.**
3. **0343, day 343, a Monday, the twenty-eighth. Cost and consequence.** **Everything after the climax is worse and the chapter has to show that it is worse and not better.** The household that owns the orchard has lost the only protection the naming bought, and the man of about fifty-seven is no better off, and the digger goes in two days whatever anybody said on Sunday. **Nobody in this chapter is a villain and nobody has been converted, and the chapter is about a subtraction and about what is on the table afterwards.**
4. **0344, day 344, a Tuesday, the twenty-ninth. Action, physical work.** **The digger goes, and puts a barrow against the end of a cut, and looks along it from the end, and does not touch it, and says one sentence, and the sentence is not an answer, and the line is not measured and not dug and no rod is put in it and nobody counts it.** **A physical-work chapter states the light, the cold, the wind and what is under a person's hands in the first paragraph.** He is eleven miles the other way and the gate is about nine hundred paces from the stone. **A man of about sixty with a handcart and a length of rope is available and is in the chapter and nobody sends him, and what he does in Chapter 0348 he has not done yet, and a chapter that puts a fence in this one has spent the volume's last image two chapters early.**
5. **0345, day 345, a Wednesday, the thirtieth. Political or procedural.** **The man of about thirty-six who holds gates on a turn, who is in this chapter and in Chapter 0338 and in no others, with a bar stood against a post, a barrow, a spade, and a bootful emptied before he answers, and with a second bar he put in himself and nobody sent for.** **The man of about thirty-four who keeps a stall is also in this chapter and his next after the climax, and the ninth line is not read aloud and not resolved and not thanked for and he is not thanked.** **A keeper is not a holder, the word *holder* is not defined, the two rolls of the same gates are not put side by side, and nobody may say what the difference is worth.**
6. **0346, day 346, a Thursday, the thirty-first. THE RESOLUTION.** **A line entered in a register in a room in daylight with a date on it and nothing under the day, and no word on it, and a thing recorded as one that may not be dug.** The register-keeper and the woman of about sixty-nine are both in this chapter and about nine people are in the room. **The man of about fifty-seven is told, in the room, what he has, and what he has is a line he cannot have shown anybody and a winter he cannot get back, and he says what it costs out loud and nobody in the room tells him he was wrong, because nobody in the room is wrong. He is not a villain in this volume and is not converted and does not leave and is not happy. The woman of about sixty-nine's sheet is not entered, not copied and not taken out of the room, because she refused that on the fifth of that month and the condition is hers and nobody may un-condition it. And the recording is the only instrument in four hundred miles that an office nine hundred miles off cannot ask to have produced, because a thing that may not be dug is a refusal and a refusal is not a return. Nobody asks anybody whether it will go.**
7. **0347, day 347, a Friday, the thirty-second. Action, physical work.** **The boards come off the wall at a shut gate, and the man of about thirty-eight who is to take them up comes up that road for the first time in about two months, and the woman of about fifty who keeps that gate is in the chapter and is asked nothing.** **A physical-work chapter states the light, the cold, the wind and what is under a person's hands in the first paragraph.** Nobody puts a name at the top of anything and nobody is sent to her.
8. **0348, day 348, a Saturday, the thirty-third. Action and political, and it is the volume's last political act.** **A man of about sixty with a handcart and a length of rope puts a fence four feet off a line nobody has measured, at the top of a road nobody has opened, and nobody sent him and nobody stops him.** **About four people have worked out that a fence four feet off a line is the most ordinary thing in the world and the most permanent, and that it will be there when neither of them is, and that neither of them ever agreed where the line was and the fence does not care.** **A fence is a political act and a chapter in which a man puts one four feet off a line nobody measured is a physical-work chapter that is also the volume's last political act, and both of those are true and the outline's count uses the first. The nineteen stones are not this fence and may not be joined to it.** A physical-work chapter states the light, the cold, the wind and what is under a person's hands in the first paragraph.
9. **0349, day 348+1, a Sunday, the thirty-fourth. Recovery.** **Tamsin Quill is in this chapter and in no other of these ten, with a folded sheet of road with about nine places on it, folded the same way every time, and the ninth line, and the consent fracture visible and not mended and nobody apologising in it, and a person of about twenty-one in a room who does not know what she is for and is not going to be told.** The road north of the Marches is shut and does not open and nobody shuts it.
10. **0350, day 350, a Monday, the thirty-fifth. THE LAST IMAGE, and it is a fence, and the day is a Monday and the volume's first day was a Monday.** **The volume ends on a Monday and there are exactly forty-nine days between its first page and its last and a hand in a cloth on the second of them.** **Nobody got stronger in fifty days. A word was put to a line in the ground in a room and it was taken back off the only page it was ever on, and the reader has been told what it is called and no page in the world can say so. And the last thing on the page is a fence put by a man nobody sent.**

---

## The prose this batch is written under

1. **A chapter may not open by summarising itself, and least of all its ending.** The opening sentence states a pressure or an arrival. It does not state the finding, and the finding is the thing the chapter is for.
2. **The recapping ledger paragraph is gone and it is not coming back in another shape. No lead paragraph of this batch carries an interval figure.**
3. **A bolded speech is the only speaker marker in this manuscript.** Within a section the bold marks one voice and the two voices alternate, and a speech may not carry two speakers in one exchange. **Bold the whole of a turn or none of it. A paragraph with a plain quotation mark at the front and a bolded quotation mark in the middle is a fault and not a style**, and Batch 0002 wrote seven chapters of it and Batch 0004 found two paragraphs of it in ten and split both with a narration beat.
4. **The measure is the share of a chapter's words inside bold marks and not marks per speech.** Volume 01 is the model at 10.4 per cent and about 35 is the ceiling. **Batch 0002 finished at 7.7 to 20.8 with a mean of 15.2; Batch 0003 finished at 7.0 to 18.4 with a mean of 13.4 in fifty spans; Batch 0004 finished at 8.8 to 19.9 with a mean of 13.5 in fifty-eight spans, and its longest bolded turn is ninety-three, and about 90 is the working ceiling and ninety-five is the hard one.** Open below 18 and check it, because a batch that writes its own measurements instead of running them publishes four wrong figures in the same run as the prose. **Batch 0004 wrote five turns over the hard ceiling and repaired all five by moving a clause into a plain paragraph and not by cutting a speech, and that is the method.**
5. **No chapter may contain more than two consecutive exchanges between the same two people**, which is four speech paragraphs. **Every card names a third party, a task or a thing carried, and the chapter's first paragraph has somebody's hands on something — Batch 0004 ran ten for ten on that, and the four physical-work chapters of this batch (0344, 0347, 0348 and one of the others) state the light, the cold, the wind and what is under a person's hands in the first paragraph.**
6. **The counting device, the *about N seconds* refrain, the *a person who does not want to be asked* refrain and the *in about nine seconds* refrain are declared motifs of this manuscript, none of them may stand twice in one chapter, and none of them may stand in a chapter whose finding is a refusal.** **Chapter 0342's finding is a subtraction and Chapter 0344's is a sentence that is not an answer, and both are close enough to a refusal that the counting devices are to stay out of both.** **THE CHORUS FRAME — *about four people in* — IS THE ONE TO WATCH, AND IT IS BETTER IN THIS VOLUME THAN IT WAS IN THE LAST THREE BATCHES AND IT MUST NOT GO BACK UP.** Batch 0001 measured about one in five paragraphs, Batch 0002 one in about three, **Batch 0003 one in two in two hundred and eighty-nine paragraphs, and Batch 0004 stripped sixty frames out of named paragraphs and kept every observation and finished at seventy-seven in two hundred and eighty-three, one in three point seven, against one in about four across Volume 06.** The cause of Batch 0003's figure is named at `bible/power-system.md` §43 item 23: chapters whose subject is a person being left alone give the narrator's one counting habit nothing else to attach itself to. **This batch has three chapters whose subject is a person being alone — 0341, 0344 and 0349 — and one chapter whose subject is a subtraction, and the frame is the first thing to watch and the measure is in the seven checks with the definition beside it. A count is not a target and the volume's cards set none; the figure is published because the figure nobody has read is not a measurement.**
7. **The people who carry the volume get a second handle beside the age and the trade and never instead of it**, and the age-and-trade form is not abolished. The handles already on a page and the same in every chapter their person is in: **the man of about thirty-four who keeps a stall and wrote the ninth line has a piece of chalk he does not use; the woman of about fifty at the shut gate has a brass key on a tarred cord in the apron pocket, a bar of ash in two brackets, a wooden hook, a piece of chalk, and a date in chalk on the post every morning with nothing rubbed out; the man of about thirty-eight with the barrow has a barrow; the man of about thirty-four at the wharf has a tally-board; the man who trades on the Open Hand board has a board; the man of about fifty-seven has a length of new rope he has not used; the woman of about sixty-nine has a tin; Tamsin Quill has a folded sheet of road with about nine places on it, folded the same way every time; Hettis Roke has a waxed slate in a case; the man of about forty-one in a very good coat has a hand inside a coat with nothing in it; the man of about thirty-six who holds gates on a turn has a bar stood against a post, a barrow, a spade, and a bootful emptied before he answers; the girl of seventeen has a plain slate, a lump of chalk and a cloth; Sera Vail has a date she has to write.** Invented in Batch 0003 and carried unchanged: the man of about fifty-two who digs has a rod he does not carry; the woman of about twenty-one has a pen with the nib ground narrow, cut down with a knife; the man of about twenty-five has a left boot mended at the front with a length of cord that is not new; the man of about forty-eight has a folding knife with a hinge that has gone stiff and does not spring; the woman of about sixty-one has a stick of hazel she carries and does not lean on. **And one this batch must not forget: the man of about thirty-four who keeps a stall is barred from every roster at his own request, and a man with a piece of chalk he does not use and no standing is the volume's climax, and the two are the same person and the chapter has to be able to say both.**
8. **And the one that is not a style instruction. Nobody gets stronger.**

## The checks, and the definitions, and the figures that reproduce

**Publish the definition or publish nothing, and run all seven and not six.** The seven and their definitions are at `outline/volume-07.md` §20. **Run the word-run check and the banned-string list across the whole of Volume 07's forty files and not inside this batch's ten.**

**Batch 0004's own figures, with the definitions beside them, and a later writer who is handed a smaller number will believe the smaller number.** The bolded share of words, measured on the ten files with the heading line included, `---` rules counted and bold marks counted as nothing: **8.8 to 19.9 per cent, a mean of 13.5, in fifty-eight spans**, against Volume 06's 6.2 to 21.8 with a mean of 13.8, Volume 01's 10.4 as the model and about 35 as the ceiling, and **the longest bolded turn in that batch is ninety-three, in Chapter 0332, and about 90 is the working ceiling and ninety-five is the hard one.** Long sentences of forty words or more: **226** across Batch 0004's ten on the definition at `state/batch-summaries/volume-06-batch-0004.md` §15, none duplicated inside a file and none across the ten. **Twenty-eight weekday tokens stand across those ten files and all twenty-eight are correct and three faults of one family were found and repaired in the writing pass.** The word-run across all forty files of Volume 07, each file's lead paragraph subtracted: a top of **fifty-five between Chapters 0321 and 0335**, and it is the rod in the hut, **a motif and not a duplication, because §17.8 requires a second handle to be the same in every chapter its person is in**; the next is forty-six between 0319 and 0338 and is the gate-keeper frame, and it is the same class of thing. **A motif and a duplication are not currently separable by any instrument in this repository and the classification is printed beside every figure for that reason.** The chorus frame, on the bare head every occurrence of *about four people in*: **seventy-seven in two hundred and eighty-three paragraphs, one in three point seven**, and **it is the one measurement in Batch 0004 that is better than the three batches before it, and it was better because sixty named frames were stripped out and every observation was kept, and the six chapters that were over the line are 0331, 0332, 0333, 0334, 0336, 0339 and 0340 and the frame is still in nine of them, so it is a thinning and not an amputation.** The exchange: **seventeen plain speeches of twenty-seven answered, sixty-three per cent, and the denominator is twenty-seven and that is the whole of the caveat**, against Volume 06's 316 of 798 at thirty-nine point six, Batch 0002's 23 of 24 and Batch 0003's 24 of 48.

**AND THE FAULT BATCH 0004 REPEATED AND PUBLISHED, because it will happen again.** Its writing pass made every edit on the file on disk, verified each edit with an assertion against the string before the write, and checked for fused words afterwards **on a vocabulary built from Chapters 0301 to 0320, which the pass did not touch, and the ten files carry zero fused words.** It repaired twenty interval figures, three weekdays, one banned string, two paragraphs carrying two speeches, three bolded narrative paragraphs, five over-long bolded turns, one chapter that opened at 2.5 per cent bold, and one broken seam left by its own chorus pass. **The rule for this run: a writing pass that edits prose with a script must make its own copy first, must verify the copy it is editing against the file it means to be editing, must treat a failed copy step as a hard failure and not as a no-op, and must check for fused words afterwards on a vocabulary built from the files the pass is not touching, because a check that counts words cannot see one.**

**AND THE FIGURES A LATER WRITER WILL QUOTE FROM THE TEN CHAPTERS THIS BATCH WRITES ARE NOT YET ON A PAGE, AND THE RULE IS THE OLD ONE: a value at a chapter boundary is derived and may be used in a chapter that dates it and may not be attributed to a chapter or to a mouth unless a page carries it.**

## The state files, after the batch

`state/current.md`, `state/continuity.md`, `state/open-threads.md` and `state/character-state.md` all name `workspace/volume-07/batch-0005/PROMPT.md` now and must all name **`workspace/volume-07/close/PROMPT.md`** when this run finishes, **and a later phase reads `state/volume-06-close.md` first and then the newest block in each of the four, and the two must not disagree.** `bible/power-system.md` gains the next free numbered section for the ten days this batch puts on a page, **which is §45, and it does not change §32, does not change §33, and does not change §33A.** `state/chapter-summaries.md` gains ten entries and `state/batch-summaries/volume-07-batch-0005.md` is written.

**AND THE ONE NEXT PHASE IS THE VOLUME 07 CLOSE, AT `workspace/volume-07/close/PROMPT.md`, AND IT IS A CLOSE AND NOT A BATCH.** It writes no chapter. It reads the finished volume and rewrites and re-verifies `state/volume-07-close.md`, which does not exist yet and which this batch does not create, and then it creates whatever the next volume needs, **and it is the only phase in this repository after an outline phase that is allowed to decide anything, and the four decisions it takes have to be written in `outline/series.md` under *DECISIONS OF RECORD* in its own words, the way the Volume 07 outline phase wrote its four.**

**AND TWO OPEN FIGURES THIS RUN MUST CARRY AND MUST NOT SETTLE.** The age of the man who trades on the Open Hand board, which is about thirty-seven in the outline and in Chapter 0309 and about thirty-nine in the prose of Volumes 02 to 06, and which Batch 0004 left as the trade and the board and no age. And the fact that the fourth of the four said no on the fourteenth of the Bare Month in a room with a date on the door, in four words, before anybody asked, and that the room on the eighteenth is Chapter 0333, in which she came to the door and did not come in, and that it is not a defeat and is not to be softened and nobody in this volume is going to ask her about it. **A batch that settles either of them in prose has decided something a batch may not decide.**

---

## What is not answered by being planned

**The boundary is not settled. The line in the orchard is not measured and not dug, and by the volume's last page it has no name at all, and the reader has been told what it was called for one day of this flood. The ninth line does not work and nobody may say whether it does. The schedule stands and the case is shut and the Regent is nine hundred miles away and is not defeated, and her one correct sentence still costs the Marches the winter road and costs the Crown nothing. The board has not been written on since day 225. The man who bought half a holding loses a season and a certainty and is right, and Chapter 0346 tells him what he has and nobody tells him he was wrong. A form with a notary's name on it and no number under the first line, and one man four hundred miles off is going to have to write a number in himself and whatever he writes will be wrong and will be his handwriting. Four people have not left in two hundred and five days and were never asked, and the word for what they are is not in this language, and a party of four goes as four, and this does not go as four, and nobody in this volume found a third way and the volume did not look for one. A man of about fifty-two who digs goes and looks at a line from the end of it and says one sentence that is not an answer, and the line is not measured and not dug and no rod is put in it and nobody counts it. A man who trades on a board has a name off it that he has never mentioned and four hundred people who can see the place where it was. And a woman of about twenty-one is in a room and does not know what she is for, and nobody in this volume is going to tell her, and that is the last thing this batch inherits and not the first.**
